how: Suffix demand counted over the 2,026 materials on disk under companies/*/world/materials; launch lines, window titles and settle times measured on a live guest booted from /mnt/storage/desktop-images/base_ubuntu_desktop.qcow2 by scripts/desktop_check.py.
contract: One entry per desktop application the `desktop` runtime adapter may open a seeded material in. `launch` is a shell template with a {path} placeholder -- or, for an application whose `opens` is empty because it opens a folder rather than a file, a {home} placeholder -- run inside the guest's own X session (never with a hard-coded DISPLAY: this image's session is :1, not :0), with `launch_by_suffix` overriding it for a format that needs different arguments. `opens` is the set of material suffixes routed to this app, and no two apps may claim the same suffix. `reader` names the reader in src/company_envs/world/desktop_app.py that reads the file back for grading, with `reader_by_suffix` overriding it per format. `window_match` is a fragment of this app's own window title, used only when the document's filename does not appear in it. `ready_seconds` bounds the wait for that window to appear; `settle_seconds` is the further wait after it does, before a screenshot shows the document rather than a half-painted frame. `cua_gym_type` names the CUA-Gym application type this entry answers, or null for an entry outside their set, so coverage is a query over this file rather than a claim in a document. `kill` is the pkill -f pattern that ends this application the way an episode does -- the controller stops the VM rather than closing windows -- so a check can prove the next launch opens the work and not a recovery dialog. It is a path fragment rather than a bare name where a bare name would also match the checker's own process. `typing` is present on an application a worker types into: `focus` is what puts a caret where typing lands (a deck has none waiting), `commit` is the keystroke that ends an entry, `save` the keystrokes that put it on disk, including the answer to any format dialog the save raises. An entry without `typing` is one where a worker's work is not typed text -- a viewer, a file manager, a media player -- and the check does not pretend otherwise.
requires_note: The launcher's dependencies, not any one app's. xdotool reads and closes windows: readiness, the window list and the covering-modal check all go through it, and it is already required by world/backends/mypcbench.py for click and type actions. wmctrl maximises the document window; this image's xdotool has no windowstate command, and sizing by pixels is wrong because _NET_WORKAREA reports the whole screen while the dock and top bar take 70 and 27 pixels of it. Both were present in the base image on 2026-09-10; a missing wmctrl leaves a window at its own size rather than failing the launch.

libreoffice_calc.name: LibreOffice Calc
libreoffice_calc.launch_note: --norestore suppresses the Document Recovery dialog that a killed LibreOffice leaves behind; without it the next launch opens a modal instead of the work. The .csv line pins the Text Import dialog's answer (comma, double quote, UTF-8, first row) so a worker sees the 183 seeded CSVs as a grid rather than an import wizard.
libreoffice_calc.reader_note: A .csv routed to Calc is still a text file on disk: 183 of the materials are, and openpyxl cannot open one. The delimited reader returns the same {kind: sheets} shape, so a grader writes one assertion for a workbook and a CSV alike.

typing.note: Return commits the cell first, and the second Return answers Keep current format, which LibreOffice raises for every non-ODF save.
The second Return answers Keep current format.

A deck has no cursor waiting in it. Tab selects the first text placeholder on the slide and Return enters it; without that, typing goes nowhere and the save still rewrites the file, so the check failed against a deck that had been saved and not edited. The two Escapes leave the text box and then the object before the save.

text_editor.name: Text Editor
text_editor.opens_note: Prose, data and mail. Source files moved to VS Code when it landed in the image: a developer role's router.py belongs in an editor with a file tree, and 7 real materials (4 .py, 2 .mjs, 1 .c) are exactly that. No suffix may be claimed twice, so this is a move, not a copy.

typing.note: gedit writes in place with no dialog.

image_viewer.name: Image Viewer
image_viewer.window_match_note: Measured on a live guest: eog's WM_NAME is 'Image Viewer' and never the file name, which lives in a client-side header bar the window manager cannot see. Every other application here titles its window after the document, so this is the only entry that needs the fallback.
image_viewer.opens_note: Vector and animation only, once GIMP landed. A .png material is something a worker is asked to change, so it routes to the editor; an .svg is not, because GIMP rasterises one on import and destroys it. All 6 real image materials are .svg and stay here. Measured: 5 of those 6 point at a remote image URL and render an empty canvas on a guest with restrict=on.

files.name: Files
files.launch_note: A folder, not a file, so the template carries {home} and no {path}: an application whose `opens` is empty is checked for {home} instead. This is the CUA-Gym `os` type's application -- how a worker finds what was seeded under Desktop/, Documents/ and Downloads/.

vs_code.name: Visual Studio Code
vs_code.launch_note: The folder first and then the file, which is what puts an explorer beside the editor rather than a lone tab. Version 1.137.0 in the image; the base image suppresses the welcome page, Copilot sign-in, workspace trust, telemetry and hot exit.

typing.note: VS Code writes in place; hot exit is suppressed in the image.

gimp.name: GIMP
gimp.reader_note: Size and format, never content: nothing here can assert what a worker painted. GIMP is openable and gradeable only on image properties, which is the honest limit.
gimp.window_match_note: Measured: GIMP titles its window '[company proof] (imported)-1.0 (RGB color 8-bit ...) 1080x720 - GIMP', so the document's stem appears but its full filename never does, and the application's own name is the only fixed fragment.

vlc.name: VLC media player
vlc.reader_note: Openable, not gradeable. A playing session leaves nothing on disk to read back, and a half-working container parser would answer 'not there' for every format it did not understand -- a silent miss dressed as a verdict. A task needing a media check needs a real media reader first.

blender.name: Blender
blender.reader_note: Openable, not gradeable. A .blend is a binary scene graph and this repo has no reader for one; the same rule as VLC applies rather than a parser that guesses.

openshot.name: OpenShot Video Editor
openshot.reader_note: An OpenShot project is JSON, so the text reader is a real content reader here: a check can name a clip's file, its position or the project's title. The .mp4 it edits belongs to VLC, because a suffix routes to one application and a video is watched more often than it is edited.
